findings.description: The countdown scrolled out of view as soon as the player scrolled to the answer options, which every question forces at phone width, and never returned. Measured top 222px then -128px. Fixed in this run: the question counter, clock and progress bar are now a sticky compact header, measured pinned at top 8px through the whole scroll.

The given panels a player reasons from rendered at 42px against 80px answer options, so the evidence was half the size of the answers; two independent testers misread a stem shape and fold-crease arrows measured 10px. Fixed in this run: stem panels match option size (66px art), and a sequence row wraps rather than scrolling so every term stays visible at once. Fold arrows now measure 16px.

When the whole-test clock reaches zero the question screen is replaced by the results screen with no message, and a click already in flight errors out. Nothing tells the player the test ended on time rather than by finishing.

The score screen shows the same 0/1 for a question answered incorrectly as for one never seen because the clock expired. The distinction appears only as a red Skipped tag inside individual review cards further down.

Moving to the next question kept the previous scroll position, dropping the player into the middle of the new puzzle with its stem above the fold. Fixed in this run: each new question starts at its top.
After locking an answer the option grid looks identical to its unlocked state, with no marking of which option was correct; correctness is conveyed only by the text banner below.

The pilot start button was enabled but did nothing when the Session label was empty: no navigation, no DOM change, no visible message, while the page's own copy described the label as inconsequential. Fixed in this run: the label is optional and a label is generated when it is left blank.

Every reveal screen asks 'Moderator: did the explanation stated before reveal match the intended relationship?', which is addressed to a second person watching. A participant sitting alone must answer a question phrased about themselves in the third person.
The Yes/No radios under the two researcher questions render as small circles set close together, below a comfortable thumb target on a phone.

The reveal banner is green for a correct answer even when the same banner reports the item took two to six times its stated time budget, so a moderator scanning quickly can miss that timing was blown.
At tablet and desktop width the pilot lays six options in four columns, stranding options E and F alone on a second row while the main test uses three columns and fills both rows evenly.

A mistyped address produced the bare framework 404 with no link, no app name and nothing clickable, leaving a visitor stranded. Fixed in this run: a not-found page naming the app, explaining the address does not exist, and linking to the test.
Restart is the smallest tappable control on the page at phone width, noticeably smaller than the primary button below it.
By-band and by-reasoning-family cards sit side by side with slightly different bottom edges at tablet and desktop widths.
The short-test button is mostly below the fold on first load at 375x812; only a sliver is visible without scrolling.
Answering the active question does not restyle its own navigator tab until the user moves on; the unanswered count updates immediately, the tab does not.
At 375px the header wraps so the word 'test' sits alone on its own line on every screen.

The dashed-circle gate tokens in machine-table puzzles are ~50-55px wide at 375px and pack 2-3 overlapping shapes; the mobile user could not read them with confidence and skipped two questions because of it.
Opening the app can land on the results screen of an earlier expired test (deadline auto-score) instead of a start page; one tap on Take another test recovers.

On one question the given-panel strip is cut off: a further panel shows only as a thin sliver at the right edge with no arrow or scroll hint. Touches the new eight-panel interleaved row — the next human pilot must check it.
On taller puzzle layouts the Next/answer controls routinely sit below the fold at phone width (10 of 44 recorded clicks needed a scroll to find their target).
